key_evidence: Meituan reports more than one million drone delivery orders and 65 urban routes as of July 2026; JD has operated logistics-drone programs since 2016.
main_risk: Route approval, landing infrastructure, safety, insurance, and weak unit economics outside dense corridors.
first_test: Run a 90-day pilot on one restricted route; compare cost per completed order, on-time rate, incident rate, and repeat use with ground delivery.
analyst_note: Best fit for a platform with demand aggregation, merchants, payments, dispatch, and location data.

key_evidence: Official policy highlights flight-operation, geographic, meteorological, electromagnetic, insurance, and risk data sharing; CAAC reports expanding flight-service coverage.
main_risk: Fragmented standards, government procurement cycles, data access, cybersecurity, and unclear willingness to pay.
first_test: Co-build a flight-risk and dispatch dashboard with one licensed operator and one local service station.
analyst_note: An asset-light entry that can support several scenarios without owning aircraft.

key_evidence: Low-altitude inspection and surveying are explicitly recognized application areas in national policy.
main_risk: Vertical-specific workflows, procurement fragmentation, hardware integration, and liability for missed defects.
first_test: Choose one asset class such as power lines or industrial parks and measure inspection cost, coverage, defect confirmation, and response time.
analyst_note: Commercial demand is clearer than consumer passenger transport, but platform fit depends on enterprise distribution and domain partners.

key_evidence: National policy names urban governance, emergency management, and medical rescue as application scenarios.
main_risk: Public procurement, mission-critical reliability, privacy, cross-agency data governance, and uncertain recurring revenue.
first_test: Pilot one event-response workflow with a city partner; define dispatch time, verified alerts, false-positive rate, and closure time.
analyst_note: Strong fit for maps, cloud, AI, and command systems; monetization is more project-based.

key_evidence: Policy explicitly identifies medical rescue and low-altitude logistics; documented drone cases show value where ground routes are slow or disrupted.
main_risk: Clinical chain-of-custody, reliability, weather, insurance, and low tolerance for failure.
first_test: Test one fixed hospital-lab or island corridor; track delivery time, temperature compliance, completion rate, and fallback use.
analyst_note: Clear value in constrained corridors, but operating safeguards must lead the rollout.

key_evidence: Passenger eVTOL companies are pursuing certified operations and demonstration sites, showing long-term potential.
main_risk: Airworthiness, operator certification, vertiport investment, public acceptance, insurance, emergency response, and capital intensity.
first_test: Conduct willingness-to-pay and route-feasibility research without committing to aircraft or infrastructure ownership.
analyst_note: High visibility does not compensate for low near-term fit and high execution risk for a general internet platform.
